**1:** The recap function, transition, and preview are present, and two of the expected section's three specific limitation examples (financial reports, medical scans) survive; only building sketches is dropped, which is within the single-item tolerance given the other two remain intact.

Limitations of Traditional Document Processing:
**1:** Both sections cover the same core argument, the same pipeline concept, and the same rigid/fragile/costly characterization with a concrete accuracy statistic.

Foundations of Multimodal LLMs:
**1:** This is the most complete version of this section seen across generations for this course: both architectures, the patch/tokenization parallel, the contrastive-learning mechanism explicitly named, all three example encoders (CLIP, OpenCLIP, SigLIP), six of the seven named current models spanning open- and closed-source, the Hybrid Approaches mention, the other-modalities extension paragraph, and the diffusion-model distinction are all present. No expected idea is missing.

Applying Multimodal LLMs to Images and PDFs:
**0:** Raw bytes, Base64, URL, and object detection are present, but object detection is demonstrated only once, directly on a PDF page -- the expected section's separate demonstration of object detection on the standard sample image (with its own captioned result) is skipped entirely rather than compressed, collapsing two distinct expected demonstrations into one. Combined with the absent multi-image comparison and separate PDF-page-display step, this section drops more than a single supporting example.

Foundations of Multimodal RAG:
**0:** The generic architecture, ColPali's OCR-bypassing role, the bag-of-embeddings representation, and the late-interaction mechanism are present, and this version is the first to name part of the expected section's specific backbone claim ('ColPali is based on the PaliGemma model'). However, the SigLIP vision-encoder half of that same claim is not connected to ColPali specifically here -- SigLIP is named only as a generic encoder example in the earlier Foundations of Multimodal LLMs section, not as part of ColPali's own composition. Since the expected section presents the PaliGemma-plus-SigLIP combination as one fact about what ColPali is built from, and only half of it is connected to ColPali here, this is scored the same way the complete omission was scored in other generations, though it is flagged as the closest any generation has come to satisfying this point.

Implementing Multimodal RAG for Images, PDFs, and Text:
**0:** The mini-project framing, the image-description workaround (naming Voyage and OpenAI's CLIP), and the indexing/search pseudocode are present. However, only the transformer-architecture query is run within this section; the complementary kitten/robot query demonstrating standard-image retrieval is not run here, the same category of gap scored in previous generations for this course.

Building Multimodal AI Agents:
**1:** The section explicitly names two ways multimodal capability can be added to agents (native multimodal inputs, and multimodal retrieval tools), matching the expected section's own two-way framing. The tool definition, agent-building code, test question, and final answer are all present, and the closing line recaps the combined skills (tools, ReAct, RAG, multimodal), matching the expected section's own closing recap.

Conclusion:
**1:** Both sections wrap up Part 1 and transition to the Part 2 capstone. The generated section recaps the OCR-to-native-processing shift rather than the expected section's specific list of combined techniques, treated as an acceptable variation as in previous generations for this course. The capstone preview matches the expected section closely, and the added video-RAG extension (see breadth_enhancement) does not displace any expected idea.

References:
**1:** Both sections contain a numbered list of references serving the same bibliographic purpose.
